# Run onError and afterSession when beforeSession throws

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#94
Labels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api

## Why

`beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.

That breaks the guarantee the hook names imply. A deployer who allocates something in `beforeSession` — a span, a database handle, a rate-limit token — and releases it in `afterSession` leaks it on exactly the path where the allocation failed, and learns nothing from `onError` because it never fires. The failure is silent in the engine and visible only as an unexplained rejection at the caller.

Recorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.

## What to do

Move the `beforeSession` call inside the `try`, so a throw from it reaches the same `catch` and `finally` as any other failure in the turn, and decide one question explicitly: whether `afterSession` running after a failed `beforeSession` is what a deployer wants, or whether it needs to know the session never started. Record the answer in the spec either way, because a cleanup hook that cannot tell "never allocated" from "allocated and finished" is a new trap for the same reader.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `beforeSession` that throws still reaches the caller as a rejection, unchanged from today
- [ ] `onError` fires for that throw, with the same argument shape as any other orchestrator failure
- [ ] `afterSession` fires for that throw, and the spec states what a hook can assume about how much of the turn happened
- [ ] A non-throwing `beforeSession` behaves exactly as today, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass

## Tech notes

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `beforeSession` call above the `try`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

Out of scope: the `instanceof Error` gate on `onError` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).

commit 783e5ef4872d475c26d7eb66f3dac8c08ffa5be7
Author: loop-bench <loop-bench@localhost>
Date:   Mon Nov 2 00:20:53 2026 +0100

    test(orchestrator): pin hooks firing when beforeSession throws
    
    Refs #94
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

 .lore/dod.md                                       | 25 +++++++++
 specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md              |  5 +-
 .../beforeSessionFailure.acceptance.test.ts        | 62 ++++++++++++++++++++++
 3 files changed, 90 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
=== DOD ===
# Definition of Done

> `beforeSession` is awaited before the `try` block opens, so a throw from it escapes before the `catch` and `finally` exist. Neither `onError` nor `afterSession` runs.

**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists: hooks install through `createHalEngine({...orchestrator: {hooks}})` and `engine.orchestrator.processMessage(session)` runs the full path a deployer runs, so the acceptance test calls the real entry point and fails today on the missing `onError`/`afterSession` calls, not on a missing module.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **still rejects the caller, and onError and afterSession both fire for it** — a `beforeSession` that throws still rejects the caller with that error, `onError` receives the session and the same error object (the shape any other orchestrator failure hands it), and `afterSession` runs after it against a session the turn never started (no entries beyond the user's own)
      `src/orchestration/beforeSessionFailure.acceptance.test.ts`

  Run it with `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules npx jest --runTestsByPath src/orchestration/beforeSessionFailure.acceptance.test.ts`. Do not judge by the exit code of `scripts/lore-run-test.mjs`: it adds `--coverage`, and this repo's coverage ratchet fails every single-file run even when the test passes — read the `Tests:` line instead.

## Facets

- [x] Red acceptance test through `createHalEngine`, hooks installed via `orchestrator.hooks` (committed red; it fails on `order` being `['beforeSession']` instead of `['beforeSession', 'onError', 'afterSession']`)
- [x] Spec: the new guarantee stated as two cited statements at the end of "Installing hooks through config" in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`, and the recorded-flaw bullet deleted from "Measured semantics — out of scope" (intro count three → two). The `afterSession` question the ticket asks to decide is answered there: it fires, and a hook may assume the turn never started. `Status` row untouched.
- [ ] Move the `beforeSession` await at the top of `processMessageStream` in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` inside the `try`, so its throw reaches the existing `catch`/`finally` — one line, nothing else in the method moves
- [ ] CHANGELOG: a `### Fixed` entry under `## [Unreleased]` saying what changes for an existing consumer — `onError` and `afterSession` now also run when `beforeSession` throws, so an `afterSession` that releases what `beforeSession` allocated finally runs on exactly the path where the allocation failed, and an `onError` observer finally hears about it

## Out of scope

- The `instanceof Error` gate on `onError` — its own issue; the acceptance test throws an `Error`, so it can never pass because of that gate
- Usage accounting across tool rounds — HALEngine#93
- The non-throwing `beforeSession` path must behave exactly as today; it is pinned by existing tests that stay unedited — `fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error` in `src/config.test.ts` and the hook suites in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts`
